metadata.case_name: WONG TSZ HO v. CHENG HOI MIN T/A KWONG YIP ELECTRIC METAL CO AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Moderate left eye chemical burn with nearly total corneal epithelial defect
source: According to a medical report by the Hong Kong Eye Hospital dated 2 October 2009, the plaintiff was first seen on 6 August 2009 on referral by A & E department of QEH. The diagnostic impression was moderate left eye chemical burn.
There was nearly total corneal epithelial defect and mild blanching of corneal limbal blood vessels.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of conjunctiva or corneal abrasion without mention of foreign body

source: According to a medical report from QEH dated 10 March 2014, the plaintiff received treatment first at the A & E department. Medical examination revealed chemical burn to his left eye and he was treated and referred to eye clinic. In addition, he also had minor chemical burn to his face and left forearm and both knees.

injuries.description: Minor chemical burn to both knees (skin burns to lower limbs)
source: According to a medical report from QEH dated 10 March 2014, the plaintiff received treatment first at the A & E department. Medical examination revealed chemical burn to his left eye and he was treated and referred to eye clinic. In addition, he also had minor chemical burn to his face and left forearm and both knees.

As for the burns to his skin, the plaintiff has not re-attended QEH for treatment. He did attend Yau Ma Tei Jockey Club General Outpatient Clinic on at least 16 times for dressing his wound from 7 August 2009 to 10 September 2009.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of knee or lower leg

injuries.description: Permanent hypertrophic/keloid scars on right side of nose, left peri-ocular region, left upper lip, right knee and thigh, and left lower limb
injuries.body_part: nose; left peri-ocular region; left upper lip; right knee and thigh; left lower limb
source: According to Dr Kong, on examination, the plaintiff had no specific complaints. He walked into the consultation room normally and did not have any specific motor or sensory defect. He commented the plaintiff as a healthy young boy. In particular, he commented on 4 areas of scarring on the plaintiff.

There is a long ‘widened’ hypertrophic/keloid scar on the right side of the nose, with a small pimple visible. The scar is slightly raised and easily palpable (felt), hence is prominent particularly when viewed at an oblique angle.
For the scars on right knee and thigh, they are hypertrophic/keloid scars. They are unsightly but do not at present cause any disability or symptoms to the plaintiff.

There are 2 scars on left lower limb, 2 & 3 centimetre in length. They are hypertrophic/keloid nature. The scars is unsightly but does not at present cause any disability or symptoms to the plaintiff.
Dr Kong is of the opinion that the scar is consistent with the injury. Given the duration since the injury is nearly 5 years, there is no regression, the scars should now be termed keloid scars.

manifestations.description: Nearly total corneal epithelial defect (ocular surface injury)
Visible scarring on right side of nose and on legs
Embarrassment and teasing leading to inconvenience to social life
Quieter and withdrawn behaviour; avoids eye contact

treatments_received: A & E treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
Referral to Hong Kong Eye Hospital
Outpatient wound dressings at Yau Ma Tei Jockey Club General Outpatient Clinic (at least 16 times from 7 August 2009 to 10 September 2009)
treatments_future: Dermabrasion or laser-resurfacing in late teens
Use of makeup concealer (as conservative measure)

losses.description: Permanent unsightly hypertrophic/keloid scars on the nose, peri-ocular region, upper lip and lower limbs
Embarrassment and teasing resulting in inconvenience to social life

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Scars on legs may affect activities such as swimming, football or basketball when wearing shorts
Nose scar may be a hindrance for employment where facial appearance is crucial (for example cabin crew or modelling)

comparable_cases.injury_description: 1st plaintiff: extensive, darkly pigmented, raised and scattered scars on the right leg; multiple scars on left calf. 2nd plaintiff: lacerations and minor bite/scratch marks.

comparable_cases.case_name: Susi Yanti & Anr v Chu Shiu-Chuen (2nd plaintiff)
comparable_cases.injury_description: Infant with 3 laceration wounds over both thighs and multiple minor bite and scratch marks over her thighs and left arm.
Circumferential first to second degree burn on right calf (5% total body surface); debridement performed; subsequent scarring but no hypertrophic scar.
Minor chemical burns on the face and a 3 cm stab wound to the right thigh; facial scar caused embarrassment and emotional effect.
